column6: In the vast ministry hall, the man walks slowly down the long centre aisle between endless rows of seated faceless clerks in black hats, holding his small paper ticket and his guitar case, looking for an empty seat; the NOW SERVING board glows amber far ahead reading 0002.

Looking up from the ministry hall floor: a jagged crack splits the high ceiling between the ducts and brass tubes, and a blade of bright blue daylight pours down onto the rows of faceless clerks, who all tilt their hats up toward it; the man stands among them, face lit by the light.

Close: the man's hands fold his small cream ticket (MINISTRY OF WAITING, 7 436 912) into a paper plane and launch it; it sails up toward the torn hole in the ceiling where blue sky and white clouds show, scraps of forms swirling. Keep the ticket lettering exactly.

The ministry hall's tall filing walls fold outward and down like a paper theatre set, revealing open blue sky and clouds on every side; the rows of seated faceless clerks and their desks are suddenly out in daylight, the brass tubes and ducts left hanging in the air.

Out in open sky on a floor of clouds, rows of faceless clerks in grey coats all lift their black hats at once in a wave on the beat; among them the man and, across the rows, the woman with her rose collar look at each other and smile; sunlight, blue sky, no machinery.

The ministry's filing walls fold back up around the hall, shutting out the last slice of blue sky; the NOW SERVING board flips to 0004; the faceless clerks settle back under their hats. Keep NOW SERVING 0004 exactly.

Close: two knitting needles click in mid-air beside her desk, knitting coloured ribbons of her laughter (rose, coral, mustard, teal) into a zigzag sweater for him; a little sewing machine stitches red-and-cream striped fabric; warm light spreading over the grey desk and the green CRT screens.

On the road laid across the clouds, the man and the woman in their colourful clothes walk hand in hand past a small milepost marked 70; smiling clouds alongside lift little hats to them; soft rainbow arcs, warm sunlight, open sky, no machinery. Keep 70 exactly.

High in open sky looking down: far below through the clouds, the grey ministry tower is pulling up out of the ground, its ducts and tubes trailing loose like roots; on the road winding up into the sky above it, the man and the woman, tiny, walk away together in their colours; warm sunlight.

Close, at the end of his row of seats in the ministry hall: the man rolls a small rose-red paper flower into a brass pneumatic capsule the size of a rolling pin, and slots it into the intake of a brass mail column; the column has a small dial of desk numbers and a little sign reading TYPING POOL; a narrow hand-width glass tube rises from the column up into the ceiling of ducts and cables. Realistic scale. Keep TYPING POOL exactly.

Looking up at the ministry ceiling: among the huge ducts, cables and brass fittings, a network of ordinary narrow glass pneumatic tubes (each a hand's width across) runs in parallel; one small brass capsule with a hint of rose-red inside is shooting along one tube in a blur of motion, far above the rows of black hats below. Realistic scale, no giant tubes.

At her desk in the ministry: a small brass capsule has just dropped out of the brass delivery bell beside her desk (a narrow hand-width glass tube comes down into the bell); the woman has opened it and holds up a small rose-red paper flower, surprised and delighted; a strip of ticker tape curls out of the capsule across the desk reading BUT I AIN'T CARRYING FLOWERS. Realistic scale. Keep BUT I AIN'T CARRYING FLOWERS exactly.
